3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Our motorcade slowly made its way towards the magnificent Benfi High Arts Center. Night was falling, and the festival was about to begin. I flipped through the brochure that had been given to us at the hotel.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: As soon as Serge opened the door, we were enveloped by the roar of the crowd.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: She nervously eyed the waiting crowd.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Since I'd refused to let her make the opening speech, her attitude toward me had changed. She now only spoke to me if I asked her a question, or if it was something important concerning the children.

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Don't worry. You're going to be fine."

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: She smiled and turned her head to look out the window once again.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Monica swallowed hard. Her eyes grew wider.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: She gave me a smile, looking somewhat comforted.

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “Are you still angry about my decision?”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: "Will you ever forgive me? I told you my reasons."

21.speaker: Monica
21.text: “I know, and I understand. It's just going to take me some time."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: She clearly did not want to pursue this topic any further.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: As soon as Serge opened the door, we were enveloped by the roar of the crowd.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: The Benfi Festival was one of the biggest events of the year. It originally marked the start of the annual religious pilgrimage, a weeks-long journey still undertaken by devout Nurists. But today it was better known as a cultural celebration that drew thousands of revelers to the city.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: As the car slowed, a coterie of reporters and security guards rushed to meet us. I turned my attention to Monica.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: We followed the guards through the cavernous white halls until we came to a set of arched doors leading to the auditorium. We waited outside as security did a quick sweep of the area, then headed in.

31.speaker: Monica
31.text: “So, this is it. I will finally stand on the same platform as you.”

32.speaker: Monica
32.text: “A platform where Sordland's women will have their voices heard and acknowledged for the first time.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “I hope this is not a mistake.”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: Monica brushed past me, took her seat in the front row and crossed her arms. I walked alone to the podium.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: The two of us proceeded to the podium. I spoke first, delivering a short paragraph about the importance of Benfi and the festival to Sordland.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: I then introduced Monica. Thunderous applause echoed around the auditorium as she stepped to the microphone. I exited the stage and found my seat.... right next to Curtan Leste.

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: I concluded by inviting Curtan Leste, the Mayor of Anrica, to the podium. I stepped down and joined Monica in the front row. Her arms were still folded.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: I spoke for just a minute, reading a paragraph my speechwriter had churned out about the importance of the festival and Benfi to Sordland.

41.speaker: Monica
41.text: “Ladies and gentlemen, as the First Lady of Sordland, I welcome all of you to the Benfi Festival.”

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: The crowd erupted again, clapping and cheering.

43.speaker: Monica
43.text: “This festival holds a very important place in all of our hearts. It is a celebration of art, music, theater -- but above all, it is a celebration of the people of Benfi, of their free and open-minded spirit."

44.speaker: Monica
44.text: “As we all unite for the festivities, we must not forget the values that have inspired them."

45.speaker: Monica
45.text: “Today marks the beginning of the Week of the Spirit. A time for vitality, growth, and new beginnings."

46.speaker: Monica
46.text: “I stand on this podium today to speak about change. About a new beginning for our society."

47.speaker: Monica
47.text: "To truly move forward, we must make a break from old traditions and strive towards equality for all. Equal rights, equal pay, equal access to education--"

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: The crowd was hanging on to her every word, but the mayor of Anrica and his entourage didn't seem as impressed.

49.speaker: Monica
49.text: “Sordland calls itself a free country. Yet half of its citizens are still barred from enjoying the same freedoms that the other half takes for granted. I refer to myself and my fellow women.”

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: A rumble went through the crowd. Scattered applause mixed with murmurs of discontent.

51.speaker: Curtan Leste
51.text: “I will not let this woman besmirch the traditions upon which our great country was built.”

52.speaker: Curtan Leste
52.text: “You are not a politician. You are not a speaker. You are merely a woman who's lucky enough to be married to the President."

53.speaker: Curtan Leste
53.text: “Your place is not at at this podium. It is at home, tending to your husband and children."

54.speaker: Curtan Leste
54.text: “Mrs. Rayne, what right do you possibly have to pass judgement on our values as Sordish citizens?”

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: The crowd was growing rowdier. Some booed and jeered at Curtan's words, others whooped in approval.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: Monica froze completely. The audience grew louder.

58.speaker: Curtan Leste
58.text: “Welcome to the first day of the Benfi Festival.”

59.speaker: Curtan Leste
59.text: “This is a night for the people of Benfi -- indeed, for the people of Sordland -- to put aside their differences and come together in celebration.”

60.speaker: Curtan Leste
60.text: “Yet as we unite for the festivities, we must remember the real reason we are gathered here.”

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: He paused for a moment to let the crowd cheer, and his eyes briefly met mine.

62.speaker: Curtan Leste
62.text: “This festival was founded around the principles of our cherished religion, Nurity. Yet over the years, it has been severed from its sacred roots and become something else. Something more perverse.”

63.speaker: Curtan Leste
63.text: “An excuse for public drunkenness and grotesque displays of the flesh. An occasion for young women to parade their bodies and engage in lascivious behavior."

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: The crowd was becoming restless. Many of the younger attendees were murmuring in disagreement, while a few of the older ones were nodding vigorously.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: The crowd fell silent. The people were giving their full attention to what he had to say.

66.speaker: Curtan Leste
66.text: “Perversion hidden under the guise of art is not befitting the beautiful city of --”

67.speaker: Monica
67.text: “Mr. Leste, it is not young women who are a disgrace to this fine festival, but you. You and your backwards, puritanical attitudes, which have been holding this country back for far too long--”

68.speaker: Monica
68.text: “Women of Sordland, we must not let people like Mr. Leste use religion as a justification to demean and oppress us. Our time has come!"

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: Shocked gasps ran through the crowd. A few people rose and applauded. Curtan Leste waited to speak.

72.speaker: Monica
72.text: “What do you mean, enough? I've barely even started."

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: I looked at the podium to see Curtan Leste's piercing gaze on me. There would surely be a price to pay for this.

74.speaker: Curtan Leste
74.text: “Mr. President, could you please control your wife before she embarrasses herself any further?"

75.speaker: Curtan Leste
75.text: “I think Mrs. Rayne is forgetting her place.”

76.speaker: Monica
76.text: "What do you think my place is, Mr. Leste? The kitchen? This festival is not about your retrograde traditions. We are living in modern times now. It's 1954.”

77.speaker: Monica
77.text: “And it isn't *your* place to decide how the people of Benfi -- especially the women -- should be celebrating their own festival."

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: The next few minutes were a blur of handshakes, photos and reporters' questions. The onlookers cheered as we walked the red carpet to the newly built arts center.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: As he went on, I could see Monica become increasingly agitated.

83.speaker: Monica
83.text: “What in the hell is he talking about? Lascivious behavior? What century does he think we live in?"

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “I don't know. Just let it be.”

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: Monica turned back to watching the speech, a frown on her face.

88.speaker: Curtan Leste
88.text: “As I said, perversion hidden under the guise of art is not be--”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “Monica, sit down. You're making a fool of yourself.”

92.speaker: Monica
92.text: “No, I will not sit down this time.”

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: Curtan Leste leaned over and hissed into my ear.

94.speaker: Curtan Leste
94.text: “Mr. President, I am afraid you have made a great mistake. There will be consequences.”

98.speaker: Curtan Leste
98.text: “No, I am merely telling what will happen. Your little stunt has lost you my support in the Assembly.”

99.speaker: Curtan Leste
99.text: "Your little stunt has lost you my support in the Assembly.”

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: I kept my eyes on the stage. When the applause subsided, Monica resumed her speech.

101.speaker: Curtan Leste
101.text: "Your little stunt has lost you my support in the Assembly.”

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “Curtan, get back in your goddamn seat!"

105.speaker: Curtan Leste
105.text: “No, Anton. I can no longer sit idly by. We are past that point."

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: The entire hall fell silent. The mayor of Anrica rose and spoke.

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Curtan turned towards the audience, speaking loudly enough to be heard without a microphone.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: Monica turned to face the audience, speaking loud enough to be heard without a microphone.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: On the front page, there was the face of Curtan Leste, mayor of Anrica. He was a Benfi native who had a longstanding relationship with the city's current mayor, and had been personally invited to make tonight's opening speech.

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: Monica's face was featured on the front page. But the schedule on the inside still said that Curtan Leste, mayor of Anrica, would be making the opening remarks. My last-minute announcement that my wife would be replacing Curtan must have caused some confusion at the print shop.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: The mayor was still standing defiantly in the front row.

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “Mr. Leste. Please calm down, take your seat, and let her finish. Now.”

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: The room immediately quieted down again.

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “Mr. Leste. Do I have to teach you basic manners? Have you forgotten what you learned in kindergarten?"

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “Thank you for the speech, Monica. You've done... enough."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: “Curtan, if you don't sit down now and let her speak, I swear I will...”

126.speaker: Curtan Leste
126.text: “Is this what you do to people who protect Sordish values? To those with different opinions? Have them removed?!”

130.speaker: Player_Italic
130.text: Order the guards to escort him out.

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: My security guards immediately surrounded Curtan and his entourage.

133.speaker: Player
133.text: “It's what I do to upstarts who fail to show restraint."

137.speaker: Curtan Leste
137.text: “Then you have just made an enemy.”

138.speaker: Curtan Leste
138.text: “Then I respectfully decline. I will not stand idly by as our Sordish values are being tested.”

139.speaker: Curtan Leste
139.text: “Especially by our very own president and his harlot of a wife.”

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: Curtan grabbed his coat and made his way to the exit. The men who had been sitting with him got up and followed him out.

141.speaker: Curtan Leste
141.text: “I will not stand idly by as our Sordish values are being tested.”

142.speaker: Curtan Leste
142.text: “Especially by our very own president and his harlot of a wife!”

143.speaker: Curtan Leste
143.text: “Do you realize what you are doing right now?”

144.speaker: Curtan Leste
144.text: “You are threatening a member of the Assembly. A member of your own party.”

146.speaker: Curtan Leste
146.text: “Congratulations, Mr. President. You have just made a new enemy.”

147.speaker: Curtan Leste
147.text: “To a mayor of Sordland. To a member of your own party...”

148.speaker: Curtan Leste
148.text: “You'll pay for this, Anton! I swear on my name.”

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: As he was being dragged out of the venue, his voice echoed in the hall.

150.speaker: Curtan Leste
150.text: “Do you hear me?! You will pay! I--"

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: The door closed behind them. The crowd began to whisper.

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "Is rudeness a Sordish value now? Is impropriety?"

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: The crowd was booing Curtan loudly now. He looked around the room and let out a deep sigh.

154.speaker: Curtan Leste
154.text: “My apologies, Mr. President. Mrs. First Lady. I crossed a line.”

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: Monica had regained her composure by now. She took her place at the microphone.

156.speaker: Monica
156.text: “My heartfelt apologies to you as well, Mr. Leste. I assure you, my intention was not to offend anyone.”

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: Curtan smiled faintly. Monica turned to the audience.

158.speaker: Monica
158.text: “I hope one day we shall all be able to set aside our differences as we have done today...”

159.speaker: Monica
159.text: “And walk towards a happier, brighter future for all of Sordland's citizens, male and female alike. We must all remember: the future cannot exist without the past.”

160.speaker: Monica
160.text: “And I believe we're witnessing the meeting of our glorious past and our bright future right here in Benfi today."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: “Vectern sis da!“. Everyone in the hall, including Curtan, finished the decades-old saying.

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: The crowd erupted in cheers. Even Curtan started clapping.

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: People started chanting Monica's name, and the band broke into the official festival anthem.

167.speaker: Player
167.text: “Is rudeness a Sordish value now? Is impropriety?”

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "Is rudeness a Sordish value now? Is impropriety?"

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “That's the last straw, Curtan -- get out of my sights immediately!"

175.speaker: Curtan Leste
175.text: "Mr. President, this is a free country. I refuse to leave."

176.speaker: Monica
176.text: “Especially a senior member of the Assembly such as yourself, who has pledged his life to the betterment of our country.”

177.speaker: Monica
177.text: “Ladies and gentlemen, I am proud to officially open the Benfi Festival.”

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “Please do not make me repeat myself.”

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: The crowd erupted in laughter. Curtan's face turned red.

181.speaker: Narrator
181.text: Monica gaped at me, looking as if she'd been slapped in the face. I leaned over to the microphone.

182.speaker: Narrator
182.text: I started walking back to my seat. Monica brushed past me.

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: I had to do something. I walked up to the stage and stood beside my wife at the podium.

185.speaker: Player_Italic
185.text: Grab her arm to stop her.

186.speaker: Player
186.text: “You knew this was going to happen.”

188.speaker: Monica
188.text: “I-- I have to go to the washroom.”

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: She stormed down the aisle and out the auditorium door.

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: She looked back at me, her face streaked with tears.

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: I wanted to follow her out. But out of presidential courtesy, I stayed in my seat until the opening ceremony concluded.

192.speaker: Narrator
192.text: I was about to leave when I felt a hand on my right shoulder. It was Curtan with a smile on his face.

193.speaker: Curtan Leste
193.text: “Thank you for having my back, sir. Rest assured that I will have yours as well.”

196.speaker: Curtan Leste
196.text: “Sometimes sacrifices need to be made for the greater good.”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “The greater good doesn't seem that great right now.”

200.speaker: Curtan Leste
200.text: “I am glad we are on the same page.”

201.speaker: Curtan Leste
201.text: “It never does. Regardless, this was necessary.”

203.speaker: Narrator
203.text: We walked out of the auditorium together.

208.speaker: Narrator
208.text: Having regained her composure, Monica stepped back behind the microphone.

209.speaker: Monica
209.text: “Ladies and gentlemen, this incident only serves to demonstrate how visibly divided our country is today.”

210.speaker: Monica
210.text: “My intention was not to offend or harm anyone. It is unfortunate that even the mention of modern ideals still does not resonate with many in Sordland.”

211.speaker: Monica
211.text: “I hope we can set aside our differences one day...”

213.speaker: Narrator
213.text: “Vectern sis da!“ Most of the audience finished the decades-old saying, but nervous whispers still emanated from around the room.

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: As Serge drove me back to the hotel, I hoped that the consequences of my actions today would not be too harsh.

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: I hoped that I could reconcile with Monica.

216.speaker: Narrator
216.text: But I knew she might never forgive me.

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: The opening event was finally finished.

219.speaker: Narrator
219.text: But I knew Curtan would never forget what happened today.

220.speaker: Narrator
220.text: The opening event was finally finished.

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: But my troubles with Curtan were not.

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “You know what, Curtan? My wife is absolutely right.”

223.speaker: Player
223.text: “I'm so sorry about this, Mr. Leste. Please finish your speech.”

224.speaker: Player
224.text: “Monica, get back in your goddamn seat!"

225.speaker: Player
225.text: “Monica, we've been over this. Now is not the time. Sit down, please.”

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: Monica looked at me, surprise registering on her face.

231.speaker: Player
231.text: “But we will take up her concerns at a later time. Please finish your speech.”

232.speaker: Player
232.text: “Your task was to give an opening speech, not a moral lecture.”

234.speaker: Player
234.text: “Now, please, get your speech over with already.”

235.speaker: Curtan Leste
235.text: “I will, Mr. President. If you'll allow it.”

236.speaker: Narrator
236.text: He looked at me threateningly before continuing.

238.speaker: Curtan Leste
238.text: “I will finish my speech if you'll allow it, Mr. President."

240.speaker: Player
240.text: “That's up to the people of Benfi, isn't it?"

241.speaker: Narrator
241.text: I turned around to look at the crowd. The people immediately started booing Curtan.

247.speaker: Narrator
247.text: He ignored them and continued with his speech.

249.speaker: Curtan Leste
249.text: “Benfi has always been a beacon of culture, tradition and religion. Many battles have been fought over this precious city."

250.speaker: Narrator
250.text: The crowd was in uproar. I had to lean over to catch Monica's next words.

251.speaker: Monica
251.text: “I'm *so* sorry, Anton. Next time, I'll stay in the kitchen.”

253.speaker: Narrator
253.text: She sat back down, seething. Curtan's voice filled the hall.

255.speaker: Curtan Leste
255.text: “Army after army has tried to claim it for their own, but we fought back and won each time.”

256.speaker: Curtan Leste
256.text: “We stand here thanks to the strong men who were able to protect their families, their lands, their way of living.”

257.speaker: Curtan Leste
257.text: “Every day, I praise God that we have succeeded so far.”

258.speaker: Narrator
258.text: Scattered applause broke out from some of the older members of the audience.

259.speaker: Curtan Leste
259.text: “Yet the traditions that form the very fabric of our society are being tested. Even as I speak!”

260.speaker: Curtan Leste
260.text: “We must stay true to our values so that Sordland can prevail. So that Benfi can prevail!”

261.speaker: Curtan Leste
261.text: “With these at the forefront, I am convinced that Sordland will continue to be the greatest nation in the world!”

262.speaker: Curtan Leste
262.text: “I invite every single one of you to celebrate our roots and our traditions at this holy Benfi Festival!”

263.speaker: Curtan Leste
263.text: “I hereby declare the festival open! Praise God! Praise Sordland! Praise Benfi!”

265.speaker: Player
265.text: “He's a bit extreme, but he is right. We owe everything to God.”

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “He sounds more like a priest than a politician.”

267.speaker: Monica
267.text: “I do not like it when the two collide.”

268.speaker: Monica
268.text: “He's a fanatic. Right or not, that's never any good.”

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: “Vectern sis da!“. Most of the people in the hall finished the decades-old saying, including me. Monica's lips moved, but she didn't say the words out loud.

272.speaker: Narrator
272.text: He exited the stage as the band struck up the official festival anthem.

273.speaker: Narrator
273.text: I spent the rest of the evening alternately watching the festivities and conversing with local politicians. By the time we got back to the hotel, I was exhausted.

274.speaker: Narrator
274.text: But thanks to the festivities still raging outside -- and the sound of Monica tossing and turning beside me -- I couldn't sleep at all.

275.speaker: Narrator
275.text: There were film screenings, concerts, theater and dance performances, art exhibitions, and celebrity-studded nightly galas. The opening ceremonies were broadcast on TV and watched by millions.

279.speaker: Narrator
279.text: The two of us glared angrily at each other.

280.speaker: Curtan Leste
280.text: “Or what? You'll have me kicked out?”

281.speaker: Player
281.text: “That is exactly what I am doing. Guards!"

282.speaker: Player
282.text: “You will stay and watch the speech. Without interrupting it.”

283.speaker: Curtan Leste
283.text: “I will not stay where I am not wanted. Clearly that's the case.”

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: Curtan's response was nearly drowned out by the booing crowd.

285.speaker: Player_Italic
285.text: Order the guards to kick him out.

286.speaker: Player
286.text: “Then you will stay and watch the speech. Without interrupting it.”

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: He tried to reply, but he was drowned out by the boos of the crowd.

289.speaker: Curtan Leste
289.text: “I will not stay where I am not wanted. Clearly that's the case.”

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: He looked around the room and let out a deep sigh.

297.speaker: Narrator
297.text: She didn't reply at all. She clearly did not want to pursue this topic any further.

333.speaker: Narrator
333.text: I had been asked to make a quick set of remarks introducing Curtan Leste. I beckoned Monica to join me on the podium.

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: The hall fell silent. Monica rose and continued.

336.speaker: Player
336.text: “I praise God he's only allowed to speak for another two minutes.”

340.speaker: Narrator
340.text: Monica said nothing, her gaze fixed forward.

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "Mr. Leste, I believe you had a speech prepared?"

351.speaker: Narrator
351.text: After some confusion, the band broke into the official festival anthem. The crowd cheered.

352.speaker: Narrator
352.text: Smiling triumphantly, Curtan strode to the podium.

354.speaker: Curtan Leste
354.text: "I'm only doing what I feel is right to protect my country."

355.speaker: Player
355.text: "You feel it's right to berate a woman? The president's wife, at that?"

356.speaker: Player
356.text: "And I feel it's right to have you thrown out. Guards!"

358.speaker: Curtan Leste
358.text: "Her ideas are dangerous, Anton. They'll lead us down a dark path."

360.speaker: Player
360.text: "Your ideas, on the other hand, will lead us back to the Dark Ages."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "Maybe they will, maybe they won't. The only thing for certain is that you won't garner sympathy by making a scene."

362.speaker: Player
362.text: "I'll show you a dark path. Guards!"

366.speaker: Player
366.text: "And without change, we are fossils. Now please, sit down."

367.speaker: Player
367.text: "My administration has not lost sight of tradition. You'll have to trust me, Curtan."

373.speaker: Curtan Leste
373.text: "Very well. I will not stay where I am clearly not wanted."

377.speaker: Monica
377.text: “And walk towards a happier, brighter future for all of Sordland's citizens, male and female alike. We must all remember: the future cannot exist without the past.”

378.speaker: Monica
378.text: “And I believe we're witnessing the meeting of our glorious past and our bright future right here in Benfi today."

379.speaker: Monica
379.text: “Ladies and gentlemen, I am proud to officially open the Benfi Festival.”

380.speaker: Narrator
380.text: I let Monica and my entourage know we'd be flying straight back to Holsord. I was in for yet another sleepless night.

407.speaker: Narrator
407.text: Since Gloria had convinced me to cancel her opening speech, things between us had been strained. She'd barely said a word to me all day.

411.speaker: Player
411.text: "I told you about what Gloria said. The change you want is coming."

412.speaker: Monica
412.text: "When, Anton? In all her time in Assembly, has she proposed even one women's rights law?"

413.speaker: Monica
413.text: "If you ask me, she's gotten a bit too comfortable being one of the only women in the men's club."

414.speaker: Monica
414.text: "Let me have a word with her after all this. I'll show her who's shrill."
